question: is the KLD measurement technique fully documented and reachable from the model cards, how does it actually differ from the other published protocols, and are the numbers credible — where would a hostile expert attack them and does the evidence hold
stance: adversarial audit, not a defence. Findings are ordered by how much they would cost us if a hostile reviewer found them first. Every number below was read from the artifact cited beside it or measured by this audit on this machine with no GPU.
hardware_note: no GPU used or required; the physical RTX 5090 was held by KvDtypeSweep throughout and was not touched
what_this_audit_ran: fetched the live published card of all 7 model repos and both dataset repos from the Hub and diffed each against its repo source file
HTTP-checked all 104 distinct URLs appearing in those published cards
enumerated the full file tree of both datasets (7,890 files at main, 5,837 at the revision the cards pin) and the tree at the pinned revision
downloaded all 79 published per-shard reports plus the parent suite manifest, the ten shard views, the ladder pin and the corpus fetch log (about 24 MB)
rebuilt all five published ten-shard cumulative receipts and the published paired receipt with tools/kld_aggregate.py on CPU
rebuilt a published two-shard tail receipt including all 562 histogram counts and every bin-bounded quantile
verified the shared BF16 head is downloadable at the digest every published report pins
diffed tools/fidelity.py function by function across the two harness digests the receipts pin and the file at repository head
re-ran the repo's own near-duplicate scanner over the full 941-document v5 corpus against the six exllamav3 calibration files
verified all 941 corpus documents on disk against the published fetch log, and all six calibration files against the digests the receipts pin
stress-tested the published bootstrap against a cluster-robust analytic interval, a BCa interval and five seeds
measured the composition and shard robustness of the published ordering from the per-context rows in the published receipts
checked that the runtime image digest the ladder pins is anonymously pullable from Docker Hub

friction_a_stranger_hits.what: the dataset card says 'run tools/kld_aggregate.py over reports/kld5/shard-*/report-<name>.json'. Run exactly that and it REJECTS.
friction_a_stranger_hits.why: the published ladder reports are schema qwen38-fidelity-report/1 (the ten-shard run predates the tail histogram, which is why the published receipts carry "tail": null), so the aggregator demands --allow-legacy-no-tail; and the ten shard views declare ten different suite_token_sha256 values, so it demands --suite to verify parent lineage
friction_a_stranger_hits.verdict: the tool is right to fail closed and the messages name the exact flags, but the documented command does not work as written. Fixed in docs/42 section 9.

friction_a_stranger_hits.what: content_sha256 cannot be reproduced by anyone, ever, not even by us from a different directory
friction_a_stranger_hits.why: the digest covers the whole payload except generated_unix, and the payload embeds the inputs map keyed by ABSOLUTE report paths, the shards[].report paths and the aggregator's own schema string. Our rebuild produced identical numbers and 499a712a6cf6e6f73e2be7c47d849600e3a164165ea4dd0f417c1f4ea1fbae06 against the published 8d56fdcfc775d87a9d77c58e048b24b4f51e3e2910dbcc68fb2c4942d6c65650; the only differing fields were the ten input paths, suite.parent.path, schema (/2 -> /3, the aggregator having since gained a scored_position_window block) and generated_unix
friction_a_stranger_hits.why_it_matters: kld_aggregate.py's own comment claims 're-running the same shard set over the same reports is a digest-comparable reproduction'. That is true only for us, on that box, at that revision. A reviewer who takes the comment at face value, fails to match the digest, and concludes the numbers do not reproduce would be wrong for the right reason.
friction_a_stranger_hits.fix: add a numbers_sha256 over the measured fields only, and extend content_sha256_excludes to inputs, shards[].report and suite.parent.path

m2_the_published_interval_stress_tested.why: a percentile cluster bootstrap on a heavy-tailed mean is the obvious place to accuse us of an interval that is too narrow
m2_the_published_interval_stress_tested.method: recomputed from the per_context_all rows inside the published receipts: (i) the published percentile cluster bootstrap, (ii) an independent cluster-robust analytic interval treating the 842 clusters as iid units, (iii) a BCa interval with jackknife acceleration over clusters
m2_the_published_interval_stress_tested.bca_diagnostics: z0 between +0.048 and +0.053, acceleration between +0.0558 and +0.0599 — mild positive skew, as expected for a KL mean
m2_the_published_interval_stress_tested.verdict: the published interval is not hiding anything. An independent analytic cluster-robust interval agrees to within 0.1 percentage point of relative width on all five candidates; a hostile statistician's preferred BCa interval is only 0.7 to 1.1 points wider and shifted slightly up. No ordering and no paired conclusion changes.
m2_the_published_interval_stress_tested.one_honest_consequence: under BCa the marginal intervals of hyd [0.0025689, 0.0030722] and k5k6 [0.0030091, 0.0035336] overlap slightly, which they do not under the published percentile interval. That is why the hydrated-versus-online claim must be made from the PAIRED receipt (-0.0004502589420525692, CI [-0.00046936758672114464, -0.00043254928793987676], 4,922 of 5,120 contexts) and never by eyeballing two marginal intervals. The cards do lead with the paired number.

seed_sensitivity.verdict: seed 1 is not cherry-picked: Monte-Carlo scatter of the endpoints is about 1/150th of the interval width

m3_how_much_of_the_ordering_survives_a_d.why: the strongest true statement we make is about ORDERING, so the audit should try to break the ordering rather than the mean

per_stratum_macro_means_10M_from_the_pub.note: hyd values are exact from the receipt; the other rows are rounded to 6 decimals from the same receipts. Spans are max/min across the five strata.

m3_how_much_of_the_ordering_survives_a_d.verdict: corpus composition alone moves an absolute mean by up to 2.00x within our own five strata, and an independent 512-context draw moves it by 3.3-4.1 % relative SD — yet the ordering is unanimous across all five strata and all ten shards. This is the concrete evidence for the boundary we claim: ordering travels, absolute magnitude does not.

rows.turboderp: 8,192 by subtitle only (docs/35:396); no stated field

rows.field: positions scored per context, and the rule
rows.ours: 2,047 of 2,048 — positions 0..2046, i.e. EVERY position including the high-entropy openings with almost no left context. 10,480,640 total
rows.llamacpp: 255 of 512. first = n_ctx/2, then process_logits(n_ctx - 1 - first) [LC:541-544, LC:616-624], so only positions 256..510 are scored and every scored position carries >=256 tokens of left context. 580 chunks x 255 = 147,900 total (docs/35:64-74). Confirmed independently at the byte level from their published pipeline_base_logits.bin size, 73,455,427,060 B (docs/35:76-80)
rows.turboderp: 65,536 positions in total (docs/35:459); per-window rule NOT STATED

rows.llamacpp: KL(BF16 || candidate), operator gated: sum over i where log p_base(i) > -16 of p_base(i)[log p_base(i) - log p_cand(i)] (docs/35:100)
rows.turboderp: NOT STATED for his protocol; docs/35:441-442 says only 'same direction of KL' when comparing his numbers to ours

rows.ours: exact, all 248,320 entries, two-pass, float32 in 24,832-entry chunks with float64 accumulation, never top-k, never truncated
rows.llamacpp: all 248,320 entries MINUS every base-side term with log p <= -16 nats, i.e. p < 1.13e-7 [LC:224-240] (docs/35:95-97, 35:183). Not the operator we call full-vocabulary

rows.ours: vLLM (pinned r34 build inside a pinned public image) for capture; offline replay in torch. GGUF rows only are captured in llama.cpp at pinned commit ece963f41b0b02d7a0d61436ae365762c073a4c8 and replayed through the same head
rows.llamacpp: stock llama.cpp CUDA, flash-attn on, f16 KV, batch/ubatch 16384, n_seq=32, on 4x-8x B200 (docs/35:21, 35:189)
rows.turboderp: NOT STATED (his qbench, not published as a protocol)

rows.ours: nonparametric percentile bootstrap over 842 SOURCE CLUSTERS, resampled with replacement, 10,000 resamples, seed 1. Paired comparisons use the same cluster bootstrap on per-context differences plus a win count
rows.llamacpp: a per-token SEM assuming i.i.d. tokens, e.g. 0.006949 +/- 0.000073 (docs/35:134-136). Tokens inside a 512-token chunk are strongly correlated, so their interval is narrower than an honest one and the two intervals must not be placed side by side
rows.turboderp: no interval. He publishes mean and median, and his mean is explicitly a tail statistic — mean/median runs 2.6-7.5 across families (docs/35:403, 35:447-449)

rows.ours: whole-document pre-exclusion before window selection on any exact NFKC-casefold 12-word shingle match against 859,426 calibration shingles, 10,772,868 corpus shingles scanned, 44 of 941 documents excluded, 897 eligible, 0 emitted-context hits. Independently re-derived from the text by this audit (m1)
rows.llamacpp: Unsloth state they deliberately do not evaluate on their own calibration data (docs/35:24-25), but the calibration set is private and no imatrix blob ships in the GGUF repo, so overlap is UNAUDITABLE (docs/35:188 D9). Asymmetry of evidence, not of intent

rows.ours: MEASURED, twice, and both are published. Cross-engine: llama.cpp versus vLLM on the SAME unquantized BF16 weights = 0.0005073550588083691 mean, 99.07 % top-1 (receipts/gguf-report-engine-floor.json). Replay-versus-live: KL(live || replayed) = 0.000654177503134738 on 6 contexts (receipts/v3-qualification-bf16.json)
rows.llamacpp: IGNORED by them, and their own logs betray it: Minimum KLD of -0.000140 and -0.000050 are impossible for an exact KL (docs/35:103-105). We measured their floor on our hardware rather than inferring it: Minimum KLD -0.000080 / -0.000056 / -0.000077 across the three GGUFs, i.e. 5.6e-5 to 8.0e-5 (receipts/wikitext-kld-run-a.json results.*.min_kld). Their protocol has no cross-engine term because both operands are in one engine
rows.turboderp: no cross-engine floor. He does publish a SYNTHETIC self floor — the BF16 reference perturbed at bf16-rounding scale — with mean 0.0052 and median 0.0007, and his 6.00 bpw point at 0.007 mean is 1.35x that floor (docs/35:419, 35:455-459). His ladder therefore runs out of resolution exactly where the good builds are

attack_our_own_numbers.rule: each item is classified MEASURED (we have a number for the effect), BOUNDED (we have a number that limits it but not on the current suite or not for every candidate), or ASSERTED (we have argued it and not measured it). Where a critic is simply right, it says so.

items.critique: teacher-forced scoring says nothing about generation
items.classification: ASSERTED — and the critic is simply right
items.what_we_have: nothing that closes it. We disclose it: docs/35:297-300 'it is text-only teacher-forced fidelity'; the cards' 'What the v5 numbers do not say' sections repeat it. The only generation-side evidence is a 70-item MMLU-Pro suite (receipts/public-capability-*.json), which is item-paired against BF16 but is three orders of magnitude smaller than the KLD evidence and its own card section admits a 70-item suite cannot certify the pre-registered bar.
items.what_a_hostile_reviewer_gets_to_say: 'you measured 10.5 million positions of something nobody asked about, and 70 items of the thing they did'
items.honest_position: correct. KLD is a cheap, high-resolution proxy chosen because it is affordable at this volume; the link to generated quality is an assumption we have not tested at anything like this resolution. It must never be phrased as a quality claim.
items.on_the_plan: P1 — widen the item-paired capability evidence, or stop letting KLD sentences sit next to quality words

items.critique: shared-head replay measures the body and not the head, so it does not measure the artifact a downloader runs
items.what_we_have: receipts/paired-head-e2e.json: body-only versus body+K6-head, paired difference -6.778619846896359e-05, CI [-9.014223019177851e-05, -4.632939580981435e-05], 74 contexts / 23 clusters — on the SUPERSEDED v2 suite, for ONE head recipe. docs/16:82-85 adds its own caveat that at 6.5e-04 replay error a 6.8e-05 effect is below what the storage format resolves and 'must be redone with fp32 captures before it is treated as settled'.
items.what_a_hostile_reviewer_gets_to_say: 'your headline number excludes a component you measured once, on a different suite, and then told yourself was unresolved'
items.honest_position: the design choice is right — otherwise every number mixes body quality with each packager's head policy — but the bound is stale. It has never been measured on v5, and it is the one delta that moves in the opposite direction to the others, so it matters for cross-protocol reading, not only for completeness.
items.on_the_plan: P1 — re-run the head-inclusive control on v5 shard 0 with --candidate-head, for at least K5/K6 and K4. One replay per candidate; the captures already exist for shard 0

items.critique: hidden-state capture at post-final-norm assumes the head is linear in what follows
items.classification: MEASURED, and it is not an assumption but a bound: 0.000654177503134738
items.what_we_have: receipts/v3-qualification-bf16.json: replaying a model against its own live logits gives mean KL(live || replayed) = 0.000654177503134738, top-1 0.9899853444064485, max 0.09134614002692976 — over SIX contexts. receipts/v3-qualification-fp32.json shows fp32 storage moves it to 0.0006249375925433911, only -4.5 %, so operand rounding is ~5 % of the gap and the rest is the two implementations' matmul ordering (docs/24:76-89).
items.what_a_hostile_reviewer_gets_to_say: 'your replay differs from the engine's own logits by 6.5e-4. Your hydrated build is 2.76e-3 and your hydrated-versus-online difference is 4.5e-4 — smaller than your own replay error. Your headline gap is inside your floor.'
items.honest_position: the reviewer is right about the ABSOLUTE numbers and wrong about the DIFFERENCES. docs/24:93-98 already states the correct reading: both arms traverse the identical replay path so the offset is common-mode, differences below ~1e-3 in absolute terms are not resolvable and the same differences measured pairwise are. But three things are genuinely weak: the floor rests on SIX contexts, it was measured on the v3 suite with the v3 harness, and it has never been restated in the v5 cards or in docs/33 or docs/35 — which publish absolute means to six decimal places without it. A reviewer would have to find docs/24, an iteration-2 document, to learn the resolution limit of an iteration-4 number.
items.on_the_plan: P0 — re-measure the replay floor on v5 with more than six contexts, and put the absolute-resolution caveat next to the absolute numbers on the cards. This is the single most attackable published claim.

items.critique: the bootstrap resamples clusters, so the interval is between-document and cannot capture between-suite variance
items.classification: MEASURED for the between-document part; BOUNDED for between-suite; the critic is right that the interval does not contain it
items.what_we_have: receipts/kld5-ladder-convergence.json measures exactly this and says so: relative interval width does NOT fall with volume (hydrated 14.6 % at 1,048,064 positions, 17.4 % at 10,480,640) because 'the estimator resamples source clusters, so its variance is dominated by between-document heterogeneity'. Between-suite is bounded from outside the interval by receipts/nvfp4-v5-measurement.json: the same six checkpoints read 2.4624986758761565x to 3.0790651709420223x apart between corrected v3 and v5, with the ordering identical. This audit adds the within-suite composition bound: up to 2.00x across our own five strata, with the ordering unanimous in all five (m3).
items.what_a_hostile_reviewer_gets_to_say: 'your [0.002540, 0.003020] describes sampling from YOUR corpus. Change the corpus and the whole interval moves by more than its own width.'
items.honest_position: entirely correct, and we say it: 'absolute KLD is suite-specific' (docs/33:121-123) and 'never put a v3 and a v5 number in the same sentence'. The interval is a between-document interval and should be read as one. The mitigation that actually works is more independent documents, which is what took the relative width from ~60 % on v3's 39 clusters to 15-20 % on v5's 842.
items.on_the_plan: P2 — say 'between-document 95 % interval' in the tables rather than '95 % interval', so nobody has to infer the scope

items.critique: 2,047 positions from a 2,048-token window says nothing about 262,144-token behaviour
items.classification: ASSERTED — the critic is simply right
items.what_we_have: nothing in this protocol. docs/33:129-130 states it plainly: 'Every window is 2,048 tokens. Long-context fidelity at 32k/64k/128k is a separate suite and remains unmeasured.' Long context is evidenced only by a different instrument — the needle receipts at 32,768 / 131,072 / 225,000 tokens and the native-context receipts — which measures retrieval, not distribution fidelity.
items.what_a_hostile_reviewer_gets_to_say: 'the context edition is sold on a 262,144-token capability and scored on a 2,048-token window'
items.honest_position: right, and it is the sharpest gap for the context build specifically. A distribution-fidelity number at 32k would cost one suite and a large card; nothing in the current evidence substitutes for it, and the needle results are not a proxy for KLD.
items.on_the_plan: P1 — a small long-context fidelity suite (e.g. 32 contexts x 32,768) would settle the objection cheaply relative to its rhetorical cost

items.critique: contamination exclusion is by exact 12-gram and lightly edited text survives
items.classification: was ASSERTED for v5; MOVED TO BOUNDED by this audit (m1)
items.what_we_have: the exact scan is confirmed from the text: the 44 documents with any exact 12-word calibration hit are exactly the 44 the manifest excluded, and 0 of the 897 eligible documents has a single hit. The fuzzy residual among the eligible 897, from the repo's own scanner: per-document maximum 5-gram containment over 256-word windows has mean 0.013179, p95 0.035714, p99 0.055556, max 0.492063; two documents at or above 0.10, one at or above 0.25, none at 0.50. The same scan had previously been run on the v3 and v4 corpora only.
items.what_a_hostile_reviewer_gets_to_say: 'exact 12-grams catch copy-paste, not the paraphrase a scraped corpus is full of'
items.honest_position: the mechanism is real and now sized: two eligible documents show >=10 % 5-gram window containment with zero exact 12-word hits, i.e. the filter did let lexically-similar text through. Both are C/Python source where shared 5-grams are language idiom. The tool itself states it 'does not detect semantic paraphrases', so semantic contamination remains unmeasured and unmeasurable by this method. And a stranger cannot check any of this, because the corpus text is not obtainable (G1).

items.critique: the KLD-to-quality link is an assumption
items.what_we_have: no calibration curve between KLD and any task metric. The two instruments coexist without a mapping: the KLD ladder (10,480,640 positions) and MMLU-Pro pass retention (70 items). docs/05:20-22 records an interpretation scale inherited from the upstream GG protocol ('<0.01 near-lossless, 0.01-0.05 good, ...') whose provenance is someone else's methodology document and which has no calibration on this model.
items.what_a_hostile_reviewer_gets_to_say: 'you rank artifacts by a quantity you have never shown predicts anything a user experiences'
items.honest_position: correct. The defensible claim is narrow: KLD ranks how closely a candidate reproduces the reference's next-token distribution on this corpus. Any sentence that turns that into 'better quality' is an inference and should be labelled as one. The inherited <0.01 / 0.01-0.05 interpretation scale should not be cited on the cards without saying whose scale it is and that it is uncalibrated here.

verdict.headline: the numbers are credible for what they are actually claimed to support, and the machinery around them is unusually strong: every published headline re-derives BIT-FOR-BIT on a CPU from published inputs, and this audit did it for all five cumulative receipts, the paired receipt and a tail receipt. The credibility problem is not the arithmetic. It is that one mandatory input (the corpus text) is not obtainable by a stranger, and that the absolute-resolution limit of the protocol lives in an iteration-2 document while the absolute numbers are printed to six decimals on iteration-4 cards.
what_the_numbers_support: the RELATIVE ORDERING of these specific artifacts — hydrated < online K5/K6 < context edition < official FP8 < K4 — on this corpus, at a 2,048-token window, through one shared BF16 head, teacher-forced, under this engine and this configuration. This audit tried to break the ordering three ways and failed: it is unanimous across all five strata, unanimous across all ten independent 512-context shards, and unchanged when the scored window is moved to 256 or 1,024 tokens of left context

the PAIRED DIFFERENCES between those artifacts, with their between-document intervals and win counts, because both arms traverse the identical capture and replay path so the implementation offset is common-mode
the statement that the interval is governed by document diversity rather than token count, which is measured rather than argued

reproducibility as a property of the artifacts themselves: the reports, the suite, the reference capture and the head are all published, digest-pinned, mutually consistent, and re-derivable without a GPU
what_the_numbers_do_not_support: any absolute magnitude to better than about 1e-3 — the replay-versus-live floor is 0.000654177503134738 and the BF16-storage systematic is about 5 % of the level
any comparison of an absolute value across suite versions: the same six checkpoints read 2.46x to 3.08x apart between corrected v3 and v5

any cross-protocol ratio against llama.cpp, turboderp or Unsloth numbers. The scoring window explains at most ~5 % of the distance; corpus, reference precision and head treatment carry the rest and only the first is sized
the quality of the head a downloader actually runs — every number is body-only by construction
generation quality, or any claim of the form 'lower KLD therefore better model'. The KLD-to-quality link is an assumption, not a measurement
behaviour at any context length other than 2,048, and specifically nothing about the 262,144-token capability the context build is sold on
anything outside the pinned determinism configuration: no CUDA graphs, no max_num_seqs > 1, no multi-chunk prefill, no other GPU or driver, nothing downstream of the logits
verdict.the_boundary_in_one_sentence: these are body-only, teacher-forced, next-token distribution distances between specific artifacts on one 941-document held-out corpus at a 2,048-token window, measured through one shared BF16 head; their ORDERING and their PAIRED DIFFERENCES are solid and reproducible to the bit, their ABSOLUTE VALUES are protocol-specific to within a factor that exceeds any gap smaller than 1e-3, and nothing in them is a statement about generated output.
where_a_hostile_expert_would_attack_firs: 1. the corpus is not obtainable, so the contamination claim is an assertion to everyone but us (G1)
2. the replay-versus-live floor, 6.5e-4 on six contexts, sits above the hydrated-versus-online paired difference of 4.5e-4 and is not cited anywhere near the absolute numbers (C3)
3. the head is excluded from every number and bounded only on a superseded 74-context suite (C2)
4. a dead collection link on all four cards, which costs nothing to fix and buys a reviewer a free shot at our care (broken_links_found)
5. the harness digest in the ladder pin does not resolve to any file at repository head, with no note saying why (tool_audit)

edits.insert: **How closely these absolute numbers may be read.** Each is a body-only replay value: both operands are projected by one shared BF16 head, and the replay path is not the engine's own logit path. Replaying a model against its own live logits measures `KL(live ‖ replayed)` = 6.54e-04 ([`receipts/v3-qualification-bf16.json`](https://github.com/malaiwah/qwen38-27b-exl3/blob/main/receipts/v3-qualification-bf16.json)), and moving hidden-state storage from BF16 to fp32 moves a candidate's KLD by 5.6 % ([`24-p0-results.md`](https://github.com/malaiwah/qwen38-27b-exl3/blob/main/docs/24-p0-results.md)). Both offsets are common-mode across candidates, so **paired differences and orderings are resolvable and absolute differences below about 1e-3 are not.** Read the paired table, not the gaps between the means.
edits.reason: gap G2 — the resolution limit is currently only in an iteration-2 document
